**Answer (recalled from the literature, not fully derived here):** $\lfloor (d-3)/2\rfloor$, equivalently $\lfloor (d-1)/2\rfloor - 1$.

**Setup.** Projecting $C\subset\mathbb{P}^{d-1}$ from a general point $q$ gives $C_q\subset\mathbb{P}^{d-2}$, a smooth elliptic curve of degree $d$. For $d\ge 5$, a general $q$ lies off the secant variety of $C$ (which has dimension 3), so the projection is an isomorphism onto its image. The image is not linearly normal, since $h^0(\mathcal{O}_{C_q}(1)) = d-1 < d$.

**Index.** The Green–Lazarsfeld index is the largest $p$ for which the property $N_p$ holds. I did not verify the value $\lfloor (d-3)/2\rfloor$ by a Koszul cohomology computation. It is the value I recall from the literature on syzygies of general projections of elliptic normal curves.

ANSWER: $\lfloor (d-3)/2 \rfloor$
